## Planning special education support across Ontario

Where in Ontario do schools serve students with disabilities and other special education needs? How does academic achievement vary across schools with different shares of students receiving support? For school-board staff planning future services, these questions can help identify where to review access to specialist staff, accessible learning materials, and designated programs. 

Ontario’s 2024–25 school records provide a starting point. They describe the share of students receiving special education services, identify some sites through special-condition codes, and report achievement at the school level. Decisions about additional support would also draw on students’ individual needs and the services already available to them.

::: {.keep-with-map}

## Reporting schools' distribution in Ontario, with designated sites in four communities

Where do district schools report special education service data, and where does the dataset identify designated sites or schools reporting that every student receives services? Figure 1 brings those locations together.

```{r prepare-data, include=FALSE}
data_file <- "ont-school-demo-info.csv"
level_names <- c("Elementary", "Secondary")

schools <- read_csv(
  data_file,
  na = c("", "NA", "SP"),
  col_types = cols_only(
    year = col_character(),
    board_number = col_character(),
    board_name = col_character(),
    board_type = col_character(),
    school_number = col_character(),
    school_special_condition_code = col_character(),
    school_level = col_character(),
    enrolment = col_double(),
    city = col_character(),
    longitude = col_double(),
    latitude = col_double(),
    percentage_of_students_receiving_special_education_services = col_double(),
    percentage_of_grade_9_students_achieving_the_provincial_standard_in_mathematics = col_double()
  )
) |>
  mutate(service_pct = percentage_of_students_receiving_special_education_services)

recent <- schools |>
  filter(year == "2024-2025") |>
  mutate(
    level = factor(school_level, levels = level_names),
    condition = school_special_condition_code,
    located = between(latitude, 41, 57) & between(longitude, -97, -73)
  )

district_schools <- recent |>
  filter(
    board_type %in% c("Pub Dist Sch Brd (E/F)", "Cath Dist Sch Brd (E/F)"),
    condition == "Not applicable",
    !is.na(level)
  )

stopifnot(
  nrow(district_schools) > 0,
  !anyNA(district_schools$school_number),
  anyDuplicated(district_schools$school_number) == 0L
)

school_data <- district_schools |>
  filter(between(service_pct, 0, 100))

n_excluded <- nrow(district_schools) - nrow(school_data)

district_points <- district_schools |>
  filter(located) |>
  sf::st_as_sf(coords = c("longitude", "latitude"), crs = 4326, remove = FALSE)

reporting_points <- district_points |>
  filter(between(service_pct, 0, 100))
```

```{r geographic-context, include=FALSE}
ontario <- ontario <- canadianmaps::PROV |>
  dplyr::filter(PRENAME == "Ontario")

albers <- st_crs(paste(
  "+proj=aea +lat_1=44 +lat_2=55 +lat_0=50",
  "+lon_0=-85 +datum=NAD83 +units=m +no_defs"
))

ontario_map <- function(lon, lat) {
  ggplot() +
    geom_sf(data = ontario, fill = "#F2F4F1",
        colour = "#ACBABE", linewidth = 0.3) +
    coord_sf(
      crs = albers, default_crs = st_crs(4326),
      xlim = lon, ylim = lat, lims_method = "box", expand = FALSE
    ) +
    theme_void(base_size = 12) +
    theme(
      plot.title.position = "plot",
      plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
      legend.position = "bottom"
    )
}

places <- tibble(
  city = c("Kenora", "Thunder Bay", "Sudbury", "Toronto", "Ottawa"),
  longitude = c(-94.46, -89.25, -80.99, -79.40, -75.68),
  latitude = c(49.78, 48.44, 46.50, 43.69, 45.38)
)
```

```{r service-density-map}
cell_size <- 100000
projected <- st_transform(reporting_points, albers)
xy <- st_coordinates(projected)

service_cells <- projected |>
  st_drop_geometry() |>
  mutate(
    column = floor(xy[, "X"] / cell_size),
    row = floor(xy[, "Y"] / cell_size),
    above_20 = service_pct > 20
  ) |>
  group_by(level) |>
  mutate(expected = mean(above_20)) |>
  ungroup() |>
  group_by(column, row) |>
  summarise(schools = n(), gap_pp = 100 * mean(above_20 - expected), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(
    gap_pp = if_else(schools >= 10, gap_pp, NA_real_),
    x = (column + 0.5) * cell_size,
    y = (row + 0.5) * cell_size
  ) |>
  st_as_sf(coords = c("x", "y"), crs = albers)

receipt_map <-ontario_map(c(-96, -73.9), c(41.4, 55.6)) +
  geom_sf(
  data = service_cells,
  aes(size = schools),
  shape = 21, fill = "orange",
  colour = "#C6D1D3", stroke = 0.3
) +
  geom_text(
    data = places, aes(longitude, latitude, label = city),
    nudge_y = 0.32, size = 3, check_overlap = TRUE
  ) +
  scale_size_area(
    name = "Reporting schools", max_size = 11,
    breaks = c(10, 50, 200, 500, 1000)
  ) +
  labs(title = "All Reporting district schools", subtitle = "Counts by 100 km cells")
```

```{r designated-and-100-percent-schools}
all_receiving <- recent |> filter(located, service_pct == 100)

full_sites <- all_receiving |>
  distinct(longitude, latitude) |>
  st_as_sf(coords = c("longitude", "latitude"), crs = 4326)

designated <- recent |>
  filter(located, condition %in% c("Deaf", "Blind", "Deaf/Blind", "Demonstration")) |>
  distinct(city, longitude, latitude)

designated_sites <- st_as_sf(designated, coords = c("longitude", "latitude"), crs = 4326)

campus_names <- c(
  Belleville = "Sir James Whitney", Brantford = "W. Ross Macdonald",
  London = "Robarts", Milton = "Ernest C. Drury"
)

site_labels <- designated |>
  group_by(city) |>
  summarise(longitude = mean(longitude), latitude = mean(latitude), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(
    campus = campus_names[city],
    label_latitude = latitude + if_else(city == "Brantford", -0.21, 0.20)
  )

sites_map <- ontario_map(c(-83.1, -74.25), c(42.55, 46.9)) +
  geom_sf(
  data = district_points,
  aes(shape = "District schools"),
  colour = "#C6D1D3", size = 0.45, alpha = 0.8
  ) +
  geom_sf(
    data = full_sites, aes(shape = "Schools with 100% reported students receiving special services"),
    colour = "#A84615", size = 2.6
  ) +
  geom_sf(
    data = designated_sites, aes(shape = "Non-standard campuses for deaf, blind, deaf/blind students"),
    colour = "#26344B", size = 4.4, stroke = 1.1
  ) +
  geom_text(
    data = site_labels, aes(longitude, label_latitude, label = campus),
    size = 3.3, check_overlap = TRUE
  ) +
  scale_shape_manual(
    values = c(
      "District schools" = 16,
      "Schools with 100% reported students receiving special services" = 16,
      "Non-standard campuses for deaf, blind, deaf/blind students" = 0
    ),
    name = NULL,
    breaks = c(
    "District schools",
    "Non-standard campuses for deaf, blind, deaf/blind students",
    "Schools with 100% reported students receiving special services"
    ),
    guide = guide_legend(
      ncol = 1,
      override.aes = list(size = c(2.6, 4.4, 2.6))
    )
  )
sites_map <- sites_map +
  coord_sf(
    crs = albers,
    default_crs = st_crs(4326),
    xlim = c(-83.1, -74.25),
    ylim = c(42.55, 46.9),
    lims_method = "box",
    expand = FALSE
  )
```

```{r special-education-maps, echo=FALSE, fig.width=10, fig.height=8, out.width="100%", fig.align="center", dpi=180}
map_panel_theme <- theme(
  legend.box = "vertical",
  plot.margin = margin(5, 12, 5, 12),
  plot.caption.position = "plot",
  plot.caption = element_text(hjust = 0, size = 10, lineheight = 1.15)
)

receipt_panel <- receipt_map + map_panel_theme

sites_panel <- sites_map +
  labs(
    title = "Schools with 100% special service rate\nand designated sites",
    subtitle = "Details in Southern Ontario",
    caption = paste(
      sprintf(
        "%d school records report 100%% students receiving special education services\nat %d locations",
        nrow(all_receiving), nrow(full_sites)
      ),
      sep = "\n"
    )
  ) +
  map_panel_theme

patchwork::wrap_plots(
  receipt_panel, sites_panel,
  ncol = 2, widths = c(1, 1.12), guides = "keep"
) +
  patchwork::plot_annotation(
    title = "Special education service reportings and designated sites",
    subtitle = paste(
      "In 2024–25, all mapped schools with 100% students receiving special education services",
      "or a designated program were in southern Ontario."
    ),
    theme = theme(
      plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 18),
      plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 11)
    )
  )
```

On the left, circle area shows how many of the 4,626 reporting district schools fall within each 100 km cell. The largest circles are around Toronto and other southern urban centres. Smaller circles across northern Ontario show that the reporting network extends well beyond those centres.

On the right, orange dots mark 24 locations represented by 25 school records reporting that every student receives special education services. Many are in the Greater Toronto Area, and two are in Sudbury. The squares mark sites non-standard campuses for deaf, blind, deaf/blind students in Belleville, Brantford, London, and Milton. For boards serving communities far from those sites, a practical follow-up is to examine what specialist support students can access locally and when they need to travel.

:::

## Schools providing various levels of special education services

From Figure 1, we explored the geographical locations of all district schools, however only a small amount of them are fully serving the students with special needs. The majority of students needing special services are spread across Ontario schools, and the following figure will show the count of schools providing services for different proportion of their students.

```{r school-count}
bin_labels <- c(
  "0",
  paste0(">", seq(0, 80, by = 10), "-", seq(10, 90, by = 10)),
  ">90-<100",
  "100"
)
bin_midpoints <- setNames(c(0, seq(5, 95, by = 10), 100), bin_labels)

school_counts <- school_data |>
  mutate(
    percentage_group = cut(
      service_pct,
      breaks = c(-Inf, seq(0, 100, by = 10)),
      labels = head(bin_labels, -1),
      right = TRUE
    ),
    percentage_group = factor(
      if_else(service_pct == 100, "100", as.character(percentage_group)),
      levels = bin_labels
    )
  ) |>
  count(percentage_group, name = "n_schools", .drop = FALSE) |>
  mutate(midpoint_pct = unname(bin_midpoints[as.character(percentage_group)]))

share_at_or_below_20 <- mean(school_data$service_pct <= 20)

ggplot(school_counts, aes(percentage_group, n_schools)) +
  geom_col(aes(fill = midpoint_pct), width = 0.74) +
  geom_text(
    aes(label = scales::comma(n_schools)),
    vjust = -0.55, size = 3.4, colour = "black"
  ) +
  scale_fill_gradient(
    name = "Percentage receiving\nservices",
    low = "#F1D3BC",
    high = "#A84615",
    limits = c(0, 100),
    breaks = seq(0, 100, by = 25),
    labels = scales::label_number(suffix = "%")
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    labels = scales::label_comma(),
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.13))
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Most schools report that 20% or fewer students receive services",
    subtitle = "Public and Catholic district schools, 2024–25",
    x = "Percentage of students receiving special education services (%)",
    y = "Number of schools",
    caption = paste0(
      scales::comma(sum(school_data$service_pct > 20)),
      " of ", scales::comma(nrow(school_data)), " schools (",
      scales::percent(1 - share_at_or_below_20, accuracy = 0.1),
      ") reported that more than 20% of their students receive special services. 
      \nExact color of each bin is based on their midpoints."
    )
  ) +
  theme(
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    legend.direction = "vertical",
    legend.title.position = "top",
    plot.caption = element_text(hjust = 0, vjust = 0)
  )
```
In 2024–25, 4,550 schools reported that at least some students received special education services, while our data covered 4,626 elementary and secondary schools in public and Catholic district boards. From the 25 records mapped in Figure 1, 12 of them appear in Figure 2’s 100% bar. The other 13 records came from consortium, hospital, or demonstration schools outside of the two boards.

The two tallest bars cover schools reporting rates above 0% through 20%. Including the 76 schools reporting zero, 3,755 schools (81.2%) were at or below 20%. Even among schools above that cutoff, nearly three quarters were in the next range, above 20% through 30%.

For school boards, this distribution shows why planning for special education support extends across the district school network. Most reporting schools serve students receiving special education services as part of a larger student population.

text

```{r grade9-math}
grade9_data <- school_data |>
  rename(math_pct = percentage_of_grade_9_students_achieving_the_provincial_standard_in_mathematics) |>
  filter(level == "Secondary", between(math_pct, 0, 100))

grade9_summary <- grade9_data |>
  mutate(
    service_band = cut(
      service_pct,
      breaks = c(0, 10, 20, 30, 40, 100),
      labels = c("0–10%", ">10–20%", ">20–30%", ">30–40%", ">40%"),
      include.lowest = TRUE
    )
  ) |>
  group_by(service_band) |>
  summarise(
    n_schools = n(),
    median_math = median(math_pct),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

grade9_axis_labels <- setNames(
  paste0(grade9_summary$service_band, "\n", grade9_summary$n_schools, " schools"),
  grade9_summary$service_band
)

ggplot(grade9_summary, aes(service_band, median_math)) +
  geom_col(fill = "#547082", width = 0.68) +
  geom_text(aes(label = paste0(median_math, "%")), vjust = -0.5, size = 3.6) +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = grade9_axis_labels) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    breaks = seq(0, 100, by = 20),
    labels = scales::label_percent(scale = 1),
    limits = c(0, 100),
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.05))
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Median Grade 9 math results are lower in groups\nwith higher service receipt",
    subtitle = "Ontario secondary district schools, 2024–25",
    x = "Share of students receiving special education services",
    y = "Grade 9 students meeting\nthe provincial math standard",
    caption = "Each bar shows the median of the school-wide Grade 9 results in its group."
  ) +
  theme(panel.grid.major.x = element_blank())
```

## 4

text
```{r service-by-year}
service_bands <- c(
  "0%", "Over 0% to 10%", "Over 10% to 20%",
  "Over 20% to under 100%", "100%"
)

service_by_year <- schools |>
  filter(
    board_type %in% c("Pub Dist Sch Brd (E/F)", "Cath Dist Sch Brd (E/F)"),
    school_special_condition_code == "Not applicable",
    school_level %in% c("Elementary", "Secondary")
  ) |>
  mutate(service_pct = if_else(
    year == "2023-2024", round(service_pct * 100, 8), service_pct
  )) |>
  filter(between(service_pct, 0, 100)) |>
  mutate(
    band = factor(case_when(
      service_pct == 0  ~ service_bands[1],
      service_pct <= 10 ~ service_bands[2],
      service_pct <= 20 ~ service_bands[3],
      service_pct < 100 ~ service_bands[4],
      TRUE              ~ service_bands[5]
    ), levels = service_bands)
  ) |>
  count(year, band, name = "n_schools", .drop = FALSE) |>
  group_by(year) |>
  mutate(share = n_schools / sum(n_schools)) |>
  ungroup()

year_counts <- service_by_year |>
  group_by(year) |>
  summarise(n_reporting = sum(n_schools), .groups = "drop")

year_labels <- setNames(
  paste0(
    sub("-20", "–", year_counts$year, fixed = TRUE),
    "\nn = ", scales::comma(year_counts$n_reporting)
  ),
  year_counts$year
)

ggplot(service_by_year, aes(year, share, fill = band)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.8, position = position_dodge2(padding = 0.08)) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    name = "Share of students receiving special education services",
    values = setNames(
      c("#F2DFD1", "#F0C7AB", "#DF9C73", "#BD734C", "#A84615"),
      service_bands
    )
  ) +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = function(x) unname(year_labels[x])) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    labels = scales::label_percent(),
    breaks = seq(0, 1, by = 0.1),
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.12))
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Special education service rates by school year",
    subtitle = "Ontario public and Catholic district schools with a reported rate",
    x = NULL, y = "Share of reporting schools",
    caption = "Each school counts once per year. The 100% group contains 7–12 schools per year."
  ) +
  guides(fill = guide_legend(nrow = 1)) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "top",
    legend.title.position = "top",
    legend.justification = "left",
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    plot.caption = element_text(hjust = 0)
  )
```
